key_insight: Rayleigh-Darcy convection enters an ultimate heat-transfer regime near Ra ≈ 4×10^5, where increasingly fine near-wall protoplumes drive nearly linear Nu–Ra scaling.
engineering_relevance: The result helps predict heat transport in porous media systems such as geothermal reservoirs, packed beds, and thermal insulation under very high driving forces.
method: 3D direct numerical simulation of Rayleigh-Darcy convection in a porous domain
Parameter sweep over Ra from 10^3 to 10^6
Analyze Nu scaling, thermal boundary-layer thickness, dissipation partition, and dominant flow length scales
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an approximately linear Nu increase across the full Ra range, with a slope change at Ra ≈ 4×10^5 and agreement within 1.24% of the extrapolated ultimate-regime prediction at high Ra.
watch_item: The identified ultimate-regime onset is based on DNS within a finite Ra window, so extrapolation beyond 10^6 should be treated cautiously.
